title: Brief me on a repository
description: Give it a GitHub repository (owner/name) and Claude explains what it is, how it is organised and where to start reading, from its description and README. Appends to briefs/repo-briefs.md. Then paste the same link into the Explorer to see the map of every file. Needs a GitHub token saved as a credential named "github" (Explorer > GitHub access does this) and an Anthropic API key saved as a credential named "anthropic" (⋯ > Credentials). Run it with the input {"repo": "pallets/click"}.
name: Brief me on a repository

config.source:
import base64


def main(input_data):
    info = input_data["info"]["body"]
    body = input_data["readme"]["body"]
    readme = base64.b64decode(body.get("content", "")).decode("utf-8", "replace") if isinstance(body, dict) else ""
    facts = [
        "Repository: " + info["full_name"],
        "Description: " + str(info.get("description")),
        "Main language: " + str(info.get("language")),
        "Stars: %s, open issues: %s" % (info.get("stargazers_count"), info.get("open_issues_count")),
        "Topics: " + ", ".join(info.get("topics", [])),
        "License: " + str((info.get("license") or {}).get("name")),
        "Default branch: " + info["default_branch"],
    ]
    return {"repo": info["full_name"], "facts": "\n".join(facts) + "\n\nREADME (cut to 12,000 characters):\n" + readme[:12000]}

config.system: You explain codebases to developers who have never seen them. Be concrete and honest about what you cannot tell from a README.
config.prompt:
Explain this repository. Use these headings: What it is; How it is organised (infer from the README, say if you are guessing); Where to start reading; What to be careful about. Under 300 words.

{{ $.facts }}
